proposals: The Spices Board should correct and republish the cumin area figures in its 2025–26 state-wise area and production table so that state rows add up to the stated national total, so the Board’s own primary table can be used without readers having to drop a column as a likely transcription artefact.

FSSAI should publish the list of its notified food-testing laboratories with the specific residue and contaminant tests, including pesticide residues and ethylene oxide, each is accredited to perform, so the 73-of-159 figure can be checked against a primary record and tracked over time.

The Spices Board should publish a concordance between the product categories in its export statistics and DGCI&S eight-digit HS codes, so its broader “chilli” figure of $1,508.94 million and series built from HS-8 lines can be reconciled rather than shown side by side.

The Spices Board should publish annual SPICED spending by component and state, including Mission Value Addition, so the ₹422.30 crore outlay and the roughly ₹130 crore paid to 45,000 beneficiaries in 2025–26 can be tied to outcomes such as India’s 0.7% share of branded blends.

The Spices Board should publish an annual count of Indian spice consignments refused, recalled or held abroad, by destination and contaminant, so the effect of the post-2024 ethylene-oxide testing mandate for Hong Kong and Singapore shipments can be judged on outcomes.
